clue.text: Sort of organs going cheap

indicators.note: to sort things is to rearrange them, so the letters of the two words that follow are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark about what kind of church organs are on sale at a bargain price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' reads as a vague 'kind of', but 'Sort' is the anagram signal and 'of' is part of the fodder: OFORGANS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Bought for next to nothing is an idiom for a very low price, as a bargain is.

clue.text: One just starting course is not so tired

explanation.surface: A remark about a first-year student who is less weary than others.
explanation.walkthrough: A British term: a first-year university student.
explanation.definitionFit: A first-year undergraduate, new to a degree; and the comparative of a word meaning lively and rested.

clue.text: I re-enlist, undergoing training ready to make a come-back

indicators.note: being trained is being reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier rejoins the army, going through training, eager to return.
explanation.definitionFit: Springy or tough, able to recover quickly from setbacks.

clue.text: Measurement — the figure's about right

indicators.note: round, so one word goes outside the other

parts.note: a statue is a sculpted figure; the 's is 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A tailor's note that the measurement of the client's shape is about right.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's height, the size of their body standing up.

clue.text: Coming from Paris, you must follow directions and run on edge

indicators.note: the French word comes after the other pieces

parts.note: N and E, north and east, are compass points
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
vous is French for you

explanation.surface: A traveller from France told to follow directions and run feels jittery.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious, jumpy and tense, as one is before an ordeal.

clue.text: One playing an unimportant role can in turn show spirit

parts.note: a cog in the machine is someone with a small part in a big organisation

indicators.note: turned round, so the word can is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor with a bit part may still show plenty of spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A French brandy, which is a distilled alcoholic drink or spirit.

clue.text: In numbers Eeyore, perhaps, and Kanga's child get instruction here

indicators.note: the animals sit inside the Roman numerals

parts.note: CL and M are Roman numerals, 150 and 1000
Eeyore is the donkey in Winnie-the-Pooh
Roo is the baby kangaroo in Winnie-the-Pooh

explanation.surface: The Pooh characters gather in numbers to learn.
explanation.walkthrough: CL and M surround ASS and ROO: C L, then ASS, ROO, then M.
explanation.definitionFit: A school room is where pupils are taught.

clue.text: Coward, one penned up in man o' war

indicators.note: in a down clue, read upwards, so the whole run is backwards

parts.note: Noel Coward, the English playwright
a lag is a convict, someone locked up

explanation.surface: The playwright Coward is shut up aboard a warship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses NOEL + LAG together. 'penned up' looks like one phrase meaning imprisoned, but 'up' is the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sailing warship of the Spanish fleets, a fighting vessel.

clue.text: A game cut short

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A card game ended early.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten a text by condensing it.

clue.text: A safari, etc, could wander here

indicators.note: letters that wander roam about, so those of the fodder move into a new order

explanation.surface: A safari and the like might roam about in this part of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could wander' rearranges ASAFARIETC; 'here' is the definition, the place where such a safari would roam, so the whole clue paints it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenya and Tanzania, the classic safari region, lie in this part of the continent, the place the clue points at.

clue.text: There's money in oil, I reckon

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words oil, I reckon

explanation.surface: Someone guesses there is a fortune to be made in the oil business.
explanation.definitionFit: The former currency of Italy, plural of lira, is a sum of cash.

clue.text: How one should not be ashamed to delay the boss

definitions.text: How one should not be ashamed

explanation.surface: Advice on dignity combined with the act of keeping the manager waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: hold up means delay, and one's head is the person in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding your chin high shows you have no shame; read literally, to keep back your chief is to stall them.

clue.text: They're intended for smoking jackets

explanation.surface: Garments meant to be worn while enjoying a cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smoking jackets' looks like one phrase, but the clue splits after 'smoking'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for cannabis cigarettes, and also short thick double-breasted coats worn by sailors.

clue.text: Memorable communication from Russia

parts.note: Red stood for Soviet Russia, after the communist flag
a letter is a written message

explanation.surface: A notable missive arrives from Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: A red-letter day is a special one, from saints' days printed in red in calendars.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a special, notable occasion, as a day to remember.

clue.text: Hankered to embrace you, we hear, but did nothing

indicators.note: one word holds another inside it, as arms embrace someone

parts.note: to hanker is to long for something

indicators.note: the word you is to be taken as spoken, a single letter that sounds the same

parts.note: said aloud, the word sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone pined for a lover but never made a move.
explanation.definitionFit: To loaf about idly on a sofa is to spend time in idleness.

clue.text: Deciding finally to take part again in fruit production

indicators.note: the last letter of the word deciding

parts.note: to re-engage is to take part once more

explanation.surface: Someone finally decides to rejoin the fruit-growing business.
explanation.definitionFit: A green variety of plum.

clue.text: A way to sit a horse

definitions.text: A way to sit a horse

parts.words: A way to sit a horse
parts.note: the riding position with one leg on each side of the saddle, as opposed to side-saddle

explanation.definitionFit: Sitting with legs on either side is the usual riding posture.

clue.text: Winning, being polite about one's upset

indicators.note: round, so one piece is placed outside the other

parts.note: suave means smoothly courteous

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: I for one plus S, one is

explanation.surface: Being courteous wins people over, even when one is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an emotion but reverses IS to SI.
explanation.definitionFit: Persuasive, as winning ways win people round.

clue.text: Article amended part of the deed

indicators.note: something amended is altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clause of a legal document has been changed.
explanation.walkthrough: A recital in a legal deed is the part setting out the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, the opening statement of facts in a conveyance is a section of it.

clue.text: Doing the rounds with a doctor, one with a speciality

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a medical degree
the Roman numeral for one
ENT, ear nose and throat, is a medical speciality

explanation.surface: A consultant on ward rounds, accompanied by a junior doctor with a specialism.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures hospital rounds, which matches the pieces; but 'Doing the rounds' is the definition, in its sense of going round about.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means surrounding or encircling, moving round on all sides.

clue.text: Not urtful, like one Venus

explanation.surface: A comic Cockney remark about a famous statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Urtful drops its H, Cockney style, so the first sense is harmless with the H dropped too. Venus de Milo is the statue without arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney for inoffensive, and lacking upper limbs, as the Venus de Milo statue is.

clue.text: Vessel housing a navy flier

indicators.note: holding inside, so one piece contains the others

parts.note: a bowl is a vessel for food
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A ship carrying a naval airman.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale owl that nests in farm buildings, a bird that flies.

clue.text: Prison official going north in the country

indicators.note: placed inside the name of the country

parts.note: Turkey, the country

explanation.surface: A jailer heads north in Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a jailer, one who turns the key.

clue.text: Though volatile, nitre can remain a salt

indicators.note: something volatile is unstable and changeable, so the letters break up and re-form

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: unstable nitre can stay a salt.
explanation.walkthrough: Saltpetre is a salt, so 'a salt' looks chemical; in fact it means an old sailor, the hero of Coleridge's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is an experienced seaman; Coleridge's poem tells of an aged seafarer.

clue.text: Choose to hear

explanation.surface: An instruction to pick something to listen to.
explanation.definitionFit: In old usage the word meant to please or wish, and also to listen, as in Shakespearean 'list, list, O list'.

clue.text: Lecture, and grow fond of the job

parts.note: to take to someone is to come to like them
a task is a job to be done

explanation.surface: Advice to give a talk and learn to love one's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lecture' here is a verb, to scold, not a university talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprimand someone sternly is to give them a telling-off.

clue.text: One working at a bank counter

definitions.text: One working at a bank counter

parts.words: One working at a bank counter
parts.note: reads as a clerk behind the bank's counter, and also as one who counts, since the old word for counting money is telling

explanation.definitionFit: A bank cashier who receives and pays out money, and literally one who counts it.

clue.text: Song-book — why you'll hear music from it

parts.note: a psalter is a book of psalms, sacred songs

indicators.note: the word why is to be taken as spoken, sounding like a single letter

parts.note: said aloud it sounds like the letter Y

explanation.surface: A hymnal, and the reason music comes out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to an ancient stringed instrument that music comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient plucked stringed instrument, so a source of tunes.
